query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: A minor substitution of Sn into FeCoNi-based HEAs will induce the formation of a secondary BCC phase, which increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain wall pinning, thereby overcoming the low coercivity limitation of single-phase FCC FeCoNi.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase FCC FeCoNi or matched FeCoNi-derived HEAs (e.g., FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8) with coercivities under 100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Add a small amount (approximately 5–10 atomic %) of Sn into the alloy composition during synthesis.
generation.conditions: Fabricate the alloy via vacuum arc-melt casting under conditions similar to those used for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx HEAs; measurements performed at room temperature using VSM or SQUID magnetometry; composition range maintained by keeping other alloying elements constant.
generation.structural_mediator: The introduction of Sn promotes the nucleation of a BCC phase (possibly with rod-like nano-precipitates) alongside the FCC phase. This microstructural change is responsible for altering the magnetic domain structure.
generation.mechanism: The BCC phase generally exhibits higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy relative to the FCC phase. Its formation increases pinning sites for magnetization reversal, thereby increasing the coercivity. The Sn-induced phase transformation modifies the energy barriers for domain wall motion, leading to an enhanced coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline single-phase FCC alloy with Hc < 100 Oe, the Sn-added alloy is predicted to exhibit a significantly higher coercivity (potentially on the order of 2×–3× increase) while maintaining a high saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: FeCoNi or FeCoNi-derived HEAs (such as FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8) synthesized without Sn addition, which display predominantly FCC structure and coercivities below 100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to FeCoNi-based HEAs with similar compositions (e.g., including CuAl additions), processed under comparable thermal and casting conditions; measurements should be conducted at similar ambient temperatures (room temperature) using standard magnetometry techniques.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative increase in coercivity is uncertain, as the relative fraction of the induced BCC phase and the detailed nano-scale morphology can depend strongly on processing parameters and exact Sn content. Also, potential formation of minor unknown phases may affect the magnetic properties in unpredictable ways.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of FeCoNi-based HEA samples under identical processing conditions: one set as a control (no Sn addition) and one set with a minor addition (approximately 5–10 atomic %) of Sn. Characterize the phase structure using X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy to confirm the presence of a BCC phase in the Sn-added samples. Perform magnetic measurements (VSM or SQUID magnetometry) to obtain hysteresis loops and extract coercivity, saturation magnetization, and other relevant parameters.
measurements: Electron microscopy (TEM/SEM) for microstructure and precipitate morphology
Magnetic hysteresis loops (via VSM or SQUID) for coercivity (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Sn-added samples do not show a statistically significant increase in coercivity (e.g., a coercivity exceeding that of the control by a measurable margin, such as doubling above ~100 Oe) and/or lack clear evidence of induced BCC phase formation, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The present work exhibits the effects of Sn addition on the magnetic properties and microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The results show all the samples consist of a mixed structure of face-centered-cubic (FCC) phase and body-centered-cubic (BCC) phase. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix. It also shows that the Curie temperatures (Tc) of the FCC phase and the saturation magnetization (Ms) of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs increase greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The thermomagnetic curves indicate that the phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K. This work provides a new idea for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs for their potential application as soft magnets to be used at high temperatures.

Zuo et al. [] found CoNiMnGa HEA shows a low saturation magnetostriction coefficient and a high Curie temperature (Tc). In our previous work [], the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA consisting of BCC and FCC phases shows good magnetic and mechanical properties, and it was found that BCC phases show a higher Ms than that of FCC phases for the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The other work of our group [] found a minor amount of Ga addition into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA can promote the formation of BCC phase and improve the Ms of the alloy, and the value of remanence (Br) and coercivity (Hc) also increases. It was reported that the addition of Sn can hinder the formation of FCC phase [] and promote the formation of BCC phase []. Therefore, in this work, a minor amount of Sn was added into the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA hoping to get a higher volume fraction of BCC phase. In this work, the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs were studied from phase constitutions to microstructure and magnetic properties. It was found that these HEAs show high Ms, low Br, and high Tc, which indicate their potential application as soft magnetic materials. This paper offers a good method for designing future high-performance soft magnet

chosen.approach: Add minor Sn/Ga to induce BCC phase in FeCoNi-based HEA
